subject: Next steps: deployment pathway & dedicated sizing for EnergyAI
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@energyai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — deployment pathway options & next steps

Hi Samir / Asha —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs we heard
- Real-time inference for customer-facing alerts (95th p99 latency target ~150ms)
- Peak TPS ~320 requests/sec; baseline 80 rps with diurnal spikes
- Typical prompt length: 120 tokens in, ~300 tokens out on average (token mix skewed to generation)
- Sensitive data requirements — privacy + SOC2 questions flagged; exploring Private VPC or Dedicated with VPC peering

Options we discussed
1) Hosted API — fastest to production; good for evaluation but may struggle to meet strict VPC/isolation needs without Dedicated or Private
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pool; best balance of latency predictability and cost control for your traffic profile
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — necessary if you require customer-managed network & HSM; longer lead time

Immediate asks / next steps
- Can you share a sample TPS-by-hour CSV and representative prompt set? (I attached a quick template.)
- Please confirm whether HSM/KMS isolation is a hard requirement for initial rollout or a phase 2 item
- We'll run a sizing strawman for Dedicated: need to confirm target sustained TPS, p95/p99 latency SLOs, concurrency per session, and token distribution

I attached a simple template (energyai_tps_profile.csv) — fill the hour buckets you have and return. We can turn around a Dedicated GPU recommendation the next business day after that.

I'll loop Karthik (infrastructure lead) once we have the CSV so he can propose GPU family/quantization options. Marissa will follow up on contracting timelines for a reserved pool.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Ben

ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap and the template. Attached is our first pass (hourly) — highlights: baseline 70–90 rps, short bursts up to ~450 rps for 10–15 minutes twice per day during batch jobs, and occasional sustained spikes (up to 600 rps) during enterprise syncs. Token distribution attached as well.

Asha flagged that KMS isolation (customer-managed keys) is required at launch for enterprise customers; HSM not required day-one but helpful later. Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 350ms.

Questions:
- For Dedicated, are we looking at a single-GPU flavor per model instance with multiplexing, or multiple GPUs per instance for large-context models?
- If we quantize to int8, what is the expected p99 impact for our token mix?

Samir

samir@energyai.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir@energyai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment pathway options & next steps

Samir — thanks for the data, that's really helpful. Looping Karthik to provide an initial Dedicated sizing strawman based on your profile. A few clarifying notes while Karthik runs numbers: 

- Good to know KMS is required day-one; we can support customer-managed KMS with Dedicated (we'll need a short security attestation and the KMS ARN)
- For bursts up to 600 rps we recommend exploring a reserved baseline pool sized for your 95th percentile (approx 320 rps) with burst capacity configured for predictable cold-starts; that keeps monthly committed costs sensible while handling peak events
- Quantization to int8 typically reduces per-token compute and memory; in our benchmarking it reduces throughput latency by ~15–30% depending on model family and sequence length — will have more precise numbers from Karthik for your token mix

Action: Karthik — can you propose 2 SKU options: 1) cost-optimized (higher multiplexing, e.g., 8–10x user concurrency on A100-80GB equivalent) and 2) latency-optimized (lower multiplexing, multi-GPU partitioning for large contexts)? Include expected sustained TPS per GPU, p95/p99 estimates, and rough monthly committed USD.

Marissa — can you confirm typical lead times for reserved pool onboarding and contract cadence (month vs quarter start)?

—Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir@energyai.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — deployment pathway options & next steps

Ben / team / Samir —

I ran a quick sizing exercise against the uploaded profile (assumed model: open-llm-2-13b baseline behavior):

Option A — Cost-optimized (preferred if tighter commit)
- GPU family: rtx-a6000 / A10 equivalent (mixed-precision friendly) or A100-40GB if you need more memory for KV cache
- Multiplexing: target 8–10 concurrent requests per GPU at your average token mix
- Sustained TPS per GPU (estimate): ~45–60 sustained rps (generation-heavy, ~300 tokens out)
- Dedicated pool sizing: to cover 95th ~320 rps → ~6–8 GPUs (reserve 8 for headroom)
- p95/p99 (est): ~140ms / ~320ms (with int8 quant + prefix caching)
- Monthly commit (approx): $XXk–$YYk per GPU depending on region and reserved term (I'll push exact $ after finance lookup)

Option B — Latency-optimized
- GPU family: A100-80GB or H100 (for multi-GPU partitioning and bigger KV caches)
- Multiplexing: 3–4x concurrency per GPU (lower than A)
- Sustained TPS per GPU: ~90–140 rps (better for short latency tails)
- Dedicated pool sizing: to cover 95th ~320 rps → ~3–4 GPUs with lower multiplexing (plus burst buffer)
- p95/p99 (est): ~90ms / ~220ms (with int8 or bfloat16, depending on kernel availability)
- Monthly commit (approx): higher than A by ~1.6–2x per GPU

Notes and recommendations
- Given your 600 rps short bursts, I recommend reserving baseline for 95th and configuring burst capacity + autoscale to handle those spikes (we can set pre-warm slots to reduce cold-start impact)
- If KMS isolation is required, Dedicated with VPC peering is the fastest path; Private on-prem would add ~6–10 weeks for deployment and network validation
- We'll run a small benchmark (2–4 hour run) after you confirm target SKU to validate those tail numbers and token costs — can do within 48 hours once we have the sample prompt set and permission to run on representative traffic

Next actions (short list)
- Samir: confirm which option (A or B) you want us to flesh into a pricing proposal, and share any blackout windows for benchmarking
- Marissa: draft reserved-pool term options (1M, 3M, 12M) and onboarding ETA — please include trial credit/window if possible
- Ben: coordinate KMS attestation doc and share the small-benchmark plan

Karthik
